$comment: Validates _source/settings.json, which is the single source of truth. Same role as _source/erd.schema.json.
title: The settings manuscript
description: The manuscript Chapter 6.2 names for the presentation group. docs/spec/_assets/tbl-settings.md is printed from it and is a generated artifact. The manuscript belongs to no language: every cell that holds Japanese is a language dictionary so that the ja/en split is data entry rather than a second copy of 1533 rows.

$comment.description: Notes for whoever edits this manuscript. JSON carries no comments, so the role declaration goes here -- one line per note, the same shape erd.json uses. Not rendered.

weekdays.description: The seven day names, INDEXED 0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday. A cell that states weekdays holds the numbers; the generator prints the names from here, so the value and the word cannot drift apart and a later edition fills in one roster rather than editing every row.

separator.description: Printed between the names of a list. ⚠️ It belongs to a language: this was first written as a plain string on the reasoning that a mark is a mark, and check 23 refused it -- 「・」 is Japanese punctuation, and an English edition joins with a comma.

none.description: Printed when the list is empty, as the document words it.

blocks.comment: Dispatched on `kind` rather than oneOf: a failing oneOf reports only that the block matched nothing, printing the whole table back at whoever edited it. if/then names the field that is actually wrong.

dayNames.description: Seven names, Sunday first. ⚠️ Exactly seven, so an index can never miss.

cell.description: One printed cell, in one of three forms: a plain string when it is printed verbatim and is the same in every language (an expression naming another key, a dash, an empty cell); a language dictionary when it holds prose; a machine value when the cell IS a value the code generators read.

index.description: This default is another key indexed by a second one: [table, byKey] means the value of `table` at the value of `byKey`. S-3 follows fontScale this way (FR-039), and stating it keeps the number in one place instead of two that can disagree.

from.description: This default is computed from the named key.

plusFrom.description: What is added after multiplying, named as another key instead of written as a number. S-2 adds three rows' worth of rulerLabelPad this way. A literal here would be the padding written a second time, and CR-200 was spent taking one such copy back out.

plusTimes.description: What `plusFrom` is multiplied by before it is added. Defaults to 1.

machine.description: A value the generators read. The printed decoration is kept as flags so the document still prints byte for byte.

pair.description: Two numbers printed as one cell: 30 x 20px. Table T-206 gives several sizes as width by height, and a cell holding both as one string is not a value a generator can read. The separator the document prints is the generator's, not a language's.

days.description: Weekdays as NUMBERS. The day names are printed from the manuscript's roster, so a cell that states weekdays never holds the words -- holding both would let them disagree. An empty list prints the roster's word for none.

encoding.description: Which of the exchange format's two weekday numberings this cell uses. ⛔ It has two, and they differ by one: WeekDay/DayType counts 1 = Sunday to 7 = Saturday (0 marks an exception day), while Project/WeekStartDay counts 0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday. AT-73 and AT-17 state both. A cell must say which, or Monday is 1 in one row and 2 in the next with nothing to tell them apart.

form.description: Which roster the names come from: the one-character form (used in a list) or the full one.

prefix.description: A phrase printed BEFORE the value, held per language. It exists so that a cell like S-90's can carry its number as a value instead of burying it in a sentence -- and the number is not written a second time inside the phrase.

num.description: The number AS WRITTEN, not a JSON number: 0.80 and 1.0 would come back as 0.8 and 1.0 and stop matching the document. The author's precision is part of the value.

lit.description: A literal the specification writes as itself. A bare word is allowed because table T-206 prints one (S-99a's `user`, the name the watermark starts from); it is still a value the code reads, not prose.

suffix.description: A unit printed after the value.

mark.description: 🔎 = the default has no recorded origin and may be chosen again. ⛔ = not stored in the document.

quote.description: The literal is a STRING. The generators quote it; the document prints it bare, because the specification writes a date as 1970-01-01 and not as '1970-01-01'. Without this flag lit would have to carry the quotes and the printed document would grow a pair it never had.

sep.description: The separator a pair is printed with, when it is not width by height. S-104's dash pattern is written 2,2, and printing it with the default separator would rewrite the document.

parts.description: What the two numbers of a pair are CALLED. The stored key holds an object, so a generator needs the names to reach the halves; without them the pair prints but never arrives in the code.

exclusive.description: The bound is OPEN: the value itself is not allowed. Written on a `min` or a `max` only. ⭐ This replaced writing `1 − ε`, which named a quantity the specification never gave a value to -- what those rows meant was 'below 1', not a particular number.

colour.description: A colour, in one of the two forms table T-236 uses: a hex triple, or an hsl() whose hue is either a number or the letter H. ⛔ H means the row FOLLOWS themeHue (S-73) and the letter is substituted when the colour is solved -- writing 214 here would copy S-73's value into 20 rows, and rule 03 forbids copying a value the specification already holds once. A row whose hue column says it does not follow states a number instead.

sameAs.description: This cell IS another row's cell. ⛔ The value is not restated: rule 03 forbids copying a value the specification already holds once, and a copy would let the two drift. The printed cell names the row it follows.

prose.description: Everything that is not a numbered settings table, verbatim: section headings, the notes between tables, and the ruler derivation table, which carries no row IDs.

lines.description: One printed line each, in order. ⚠️ A line that carries Japanese is PRINTED PROSE, so Chapter 6.2 requires it to be a language dictionary; a line that carries none -- a blank line, `**Type**: SECTION`, a table rule -- belongs to no language and stays a plain string. The pattern on the plain form is what enforces the split: it admits no character in the Japanese ranges, so prose cannot be left bare.

field.description: The English name the cells of this column are keyed by. 値 is one field even though table T-206 uses that column for what the value IS while the T-211 shape uses it for the value itself; telling those apart is a promotion, not a rename. light / dark / hue belong to table T-236 alone: a colour is ONE decision with two renderings, so the pair is one ROW with two cells rather than two tables whose rows could silently drift apart, and hue says whether the row follows themeHue (S-73) or is fixed.

separator.description: The alignment row, verbatim: the columns are not all aligned the same way and the printed document has to come back byte for byte.

json.description: The machine type, in the same shape erd.json gives an entity column. Stated only for a row whose printed 型 cell is written for a person and cannot be machine-read.
